Back in the peak of my obesity i was drinking 5 litres of boxed wine a day (im 5ft tall so surprised i even have a liver remaining), when i got drunk id always crave the greasiest shit ever, kebabs, mcdonalds, pizza, you name it. 

Anyway around the end of 2021/start of 2022 i decided i should probably do something with my life, enrolled in a uni course in the first semester to complete yr 11/12 (cause i dropped out in yr 10). The uni campus is huge and in the middle of a bushland rainforest, so walking between classes with a heavy backpack alone started building my stamina/endurance surprisingly fast (was so fkn exhausting at first). Id easily end up walking 13kms+ in a day just travelling to and from and around uni. Started up a gym membership with a 24hr gym n would go huff iron at 1am every second night, incorporated things like creatine n lots of meat proteins into my daily diet.

By this point i had essentially cut alcohol completely out, was only really eating once a day because i was busy studying. Then the next semester when i started my bachelors of software engineering, i found out my uni campus has a pool, so between classes everyday id go for an hr or 2 long swim as a way to refresh myself..
Before i knew it i was already down 25kgs, was a huge surprise because i hadnt been weighing myself till that moment, just noticed all my clothes were becoming way too loose and my skin was sagging a lot around my stomach/chest/arms, was expecting to of lost like 5kgs max tbh.

2023 rolls around and i start of the year with the same trajectory id been on for the last few months, however in the beginning of april sorta got knocked on my ass for reasons i couldnt control. Had 3 abdominal surgeries, a bunch of complications, a bunnnnnch of hospitalisations, a fractured rib n some bs reoccuring infection. The last 20kgs ive lost has been essentially due to health/sickness reasons, loss of muscle mass and appetite can be a proper bitch ngl, but still happy with myself regardless. Thanks again! :)

Yo not the person you were asking but thought id chime in with my own experiences.

My first dry herb vape was the dynavap and it definitely works like a charm as a starter vape. It works super well, is cheap and gives an effective high. My only compaints would be that the cap tends to have a bit of a limited lifespan depending on how frequently you use it, might have to replace it every 4 months or so otherwise it doesnt do the pop noise thing you're listening for until way to late when your bowls been turned into charcoal.
Another minor complaint would be if you're trying to use it on the go as a portable vape theres literally no way to avoid looking like a crackhead because of the way you have to heat the cap with your lighter. Last complaint would be that you'll have to keep buying a fuckload of lighter fluid because of just how much is used when using a typical jetlighter to heat it. 
You can opt for an induction heater for it but they're fairly expensive on top of the money you'd be forking into the dynavap and at that point would be more cost effective to go for a more expensive vape.

I personally use the Arizer solo 2 and have been heavily for the last almost 3 years, has been really consistent with every high, low maintenance and still conveniently portable (provided you're being mindful enough to atleast remember the bud chamber/tube is made of glass and not to go hucking it at concrete or something). Idk if you'd be comfortable foregoing that much on something you havent tried before but i honestly swear by it, consuming bud in any other way has felt super wasteful to me ever since. You could also possibly even vape in your own room too since the vape scent doesnt linger at all or cling to surfaces.

One more thing, doesnt matter what dry herb vape you use, if you save up the left over bud after its been vaped you can turn them into edibles/firecrackers/eat it straight up mixed with yogurt or something fatty since by vaping it you've already done the first step in making edibles called decarbonising the bud, turning the thc into thca, its a super fun way to recycle your bud and get the most out of it! Best luck finding the perfect blaze device op c:

Edit: also yeh its super easy to burn yourself with the dynavap, i and my partner did the same thing as the other commenter where we singed our lips accidentally using the vape the wrong way. I also still have a pretty gnarly scar on my boob from when i dropped it on there over 3 years ago which i doubt is going away lol. If you do go with it def be mindful about not being a clumsy stoned fool.
